name: Bombay Veg Sandwich
cuisine: Mumbai street food (Maharashtrian; the Mumbai roadside grilled sandwich)

ingredients.name: Beetroot (chukandar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small piece, size of a walnut

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 3 thin slices of a small tomato

ingredients.name: Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small pinch, for the chutney

equipment: Small pan or pressure cooker for boiling the potato and beetroot
Chutney grinder or small mixer jar
Knife and board, small spoon, small bowl for the chutney, a plate

steps.title: Wash the potato and beetroot
steps.text: Rinse 50 g potato and 25 g beetroot under tap water and scrub the skins.
steps.visualCue: The water runs clear and no soil is left on the skin
steps.cameraCheck: The washed potato and beetroot in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Rinsing the potato and beetroot under a tap.
steps.watchOut: Cutting them before boiling, which lets them soak up water and turn mushy; boil them whole.

steps.title: Boil the potato and beetroot
steps.text: Put them in a small pan or cooker with enough water to cover, a pinch of salt in the water, and boil until a knife slides in. In a pressure cooker, 3 to 4 whistles is a common rule (not sourced; check by feel). In a pan, 15–20 min.
steps.tip: Boil a few extra potatoes for tomorrow's sabzi and cut the cooking time next time.
steps.visualCue: A knife or fork goes in without force and the skin starts to wrinkle
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the potato and beetroot on the stove
steps.videoShot: Water bubbling around a potato in a small pan.
steps.watchOut: Over-boiling, which makes the potato fall apart and difficult to slice; take it out as soon as the knife slides in. If it is still hard in the middle, boil 5 min more.

steps.title: Wash the chutney herbs
steps.text: Rinse 10 g coriander leaves, 2 g mint leaves and 1 small green chilli.
steps.visualCue: The leaves are clean and bright green, with no sand at the bottom of the bowl
steps.cameraCheck: The washed herbs in a sieve
steps.videoShot: Coriander and mint under running water.
steps.watchOut: Wet leaves that dilute the chutney and make the bread soggy; shake them dry before blending.

steps.title: Blend the green chutney
steps.text: Put the coriander, mint, the green chilli (with the seeds removed if you want it mild), 3 ml lemon juice (½ tsp), 0.3 g salt and 15 ml water into a small mixer jar and blend into a thick paste.
steps.tip: Chutney that is too hot can be rescued with a little extra coriander.
steps.visualCue: A thick, bright-green paste that holds on a spoon and does not run off
steps.cameraCheck: The finished chutney on a spoon
steps.videoShot: Green chutney being scooped from the mixer jar.
steps.watchOut: Too much water, which gives a runny chutney that soaks the bread and makes it soggy; add water 1 tsp at a time and stop as soon as it blends. Too thin already? Add a few more coriander leaves.

steps.title: Slice the cucumber
steps.text: Cut 30 g cucumber into thin rounds, about 2–3 mm thick (5–6 slices).
steps.visualCue: Even, see-through green discs that bend slightly
steps.cameraCheck: The cucumber slices on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing cucumber into thin discs.
steps.watchOut: Thick slices, which make the sandwich bulge and slip; slice thin and evenly. Peel only if the skin is waxy or bitter.

steps.title: Slice the tomato
steps.text: Cut 30 g of a firm tomato into thin slices, about 3 mm thick, and pat them dry with a tissue.
steps.visualCue: Whole slices that keep their shape, with the seeds mostly left in the slice
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato slices on a tissue
steps.videoShot: A sharp knife slicing a tomato.
steps.watchOut: Overripe, watery tomato, which makes the bread soggy; use a firm one and press the slices on a tissue to remove the juice.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Cut 15 g onion into thin rings.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even rings that fall apart when separated
steps.cameraCheck: The onion rings on the board
steps.videoShot: Onion being sliced into thin rings.
steps.watchOut: Thick onion rings that make the sandwich sharp and difficult to bite through; slice thin or skip the onion.

steps.title: Cool and peel the boiled vegetables
steps.text: Take out the potato and beetroot, let them cool until you can hold them (about 10 min), then peel off the skin with your fingers.
steps.visualCue: The skins slip off easily and the flesh is firm and cool, not steaming
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled potato and beetroot on the board
steps.videoShot: Skin peeling off a boiled beetroot.
steps.watchOut: Cutting while still hot, because hot potato slices break into crumbs and the butter melts into the bread; wait till cool. Stains from the beetroot on the board and hands wash off with a little lemon and water.

steps.title: Slice the potato and beetroot
steps.text: Cut the potato (40 g) and beetroot (20 g) into thin slices, about 3 mm thick.
steps.visualCue: Whole, neat slices with a smooth cut face
steps.cameraCheck: The slices of potato and beetroot in two small piles
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting a boiled potato into thin slices.
steps.watchOut: Slices that crumble, which means the potato was still warm or over-boiled; let it cool further, or mash it lightly and spread it as a layer.

steps.title: Butter the bread
steps.text: Lay 2 slices of bread on a plate. Spread 5 g of soft butter (1 tsp) on one side of each slice, edge to edge.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even yellow layer reaching all four edges, with no bare spots
steps.cameraCheck: The two slices buttered side up
steps.videoShot: Butter being spread over a slice of bread.
steps.watchOut: Cold, hard butter, which tears the bread; leave it out for 10 min or microwave it for 5 seconds. Butter also helps stop the chutney soaking in, so do not skip it.

steps.title: Spread the chutney
steps.text: Spread about half of the chutney (about 1 tsp) over the butter on one slice only. Keep the other half for serving.
steps.visualCue: A thin green layer over the whole slice, with the butter showing at the very edges
steps.cameraCheck: The chutney slice next to the plain buttered slice
steps.videoShot: Green chutney being spread on a slice.
steps.watchOut: Too much chutney, which squeezes out of the sides and makes the bread wet; one thin layer is enough.

steps.title: Layer the potato and beetroot
steps.text: On the chutney slice, lay the potato slices in a single layer, sprinkle about ¼ tsp of the masala (0.5 g), then lay the beetroot slices on top.
steps.visualCue: A neat pale-yellow layer with purple slices on top, no gaps
steps.cameraCheck: The sandwich open with the potato and beetroot layers
steps.videoShot: Potato and beetroot slices being laid on the slice.
steps.watchOut: Gaps at the corners, which leave the sandwich thin and the filling slides out; trim and fit slices to the corners.

steps.title: Add the cucumber, tomato and onion
steps.text: Lay the cucumber, then the tomato, then the onion on top, and sprinkle the remaining ¼ tsp masala (0.5 g).
steps.visualCue: A tidy stack of green, red and white layers with masala dusted on top
steps.cameraCheck: The open sandwich with all the vegetable layers
steps.videoShot: Cucumber, tomato and onion being stacked.
steps.watchOut: Putting the tomato directly against the bread, because the juice soaks in; keep the tomato in the middle of the stack, between cucumber and onion.

steps.title: Close and press
steps.text: Place the second buttered slice on top, butter side down, and press lightly with your palm. Spread a thin layer (about 1 g, a thin smear) of butter on the outside of the top slice.
steps.visualCue: The sandwich sits flat and holds together when you lift it gently
steps.cameraCheck: The closed sandwich on the plate
steps.videoShot: Closing the sandwich and pressing it down with a hand.
steps.watchOut: Pressing hard, which squeezes the filling out of the sides; a light press is enough.

steps.title: Grill the sandwich
steps.text: Heat a sandwich griller, or a tawa on medium-low heat. Butter the bottom side (about 2–3 g) and place the sandwich in. Close the griller, or press with a plate on the tawa. Grill 3–4 min, flip, and grill 2 min more on the other side (tawa). In a griller, grill 4–5 min.
steps.tip: Check the underside after 2 min by lifting a corner.
steps.visualCue: The bread turns golden brown with darker grill marks, and there is a buttery toasted smell and a light sizzle
steps.cameraCheck: The golden sandwich in the pan or griller
steps.videoShot: A sandwich sizzling on a tawa, then being flipped.
steps.watchOut: Heat that is too high, which burns the outside before the vegetables warm up (black marks and a burnt smell); turn the heat down and flip earlier. If the first side is too pale, give it one more minute.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Move the sandwich to a board, rest it for 30 seconds, then cut it diagonally into 2 triangles. Serve hot with the remaining green chutney and ketchup if you like.
steps.visualCue: Crisp golden edges and neat layers of yellow, purple, green and red showing at the cut
steps.cameraCheck: The two triangles on a plate showing the layers
steps.videoShot: Knife cutting the toasted sandwich diagonally.
steps.watchOut: Cutting straight away with a blunt knife, which squashes the layers; rest 30 seconds and use a serrated or very sharp knife.
steps.funFact: Wikipedia says the Bombay sandwich became common street food in the 1960s and may have been invented by migrant textile workers, though the origin is uncertain.

reasons: it has real vegetables (potato, beetroot, cucumber, tomato) and no frying, no cholesterol-heavy ingredient and only about 32 mg cholesterol. Points off because the base is refined white bread, the butter gives about 8 g saturated fat (36% of the daily limit), fibre is only about 3.5 g and protein only about 7 g (est.). Restaurant versions usually use more butter, cheese and ketchup, so they are heavier, saltier and higher in saturated fat (est.).

researchRating.basis: one of Mumbai's best-known street foods, carried by almost every major Indian recipe site and described in food articles as a Mumbai icon. Points off because the recipe pages could not be opened here, so star counts and reviews could not be read, and because it depends on fresh, hot grilling, which delivery versions often miss. The number is an estimate from how widely and warmly it is covered.

storage: Best not stored once assembled; the bread goes soft within an hour. If you must, wrap a cooled sandwich in foil and keep it in the fridge for up to 1 day (est., not sourced), then re-grill. Freezing is not recommended (soggy vegetables). Store the chutney in a clean closed jar in the fridge for a few days (est., not sourced), and boiled potato and beetroot in the fridge for 1–2 days (est.). Reheat on a tawa on low heat for 2–3 min per side, not in a microwave.
leftoverRemix: Bombay sandwich toast. If you have a few veg layers left, mash the potato and beetroot with the chutney and masala and spread it on a slice of toast, top with cucumber and sev (a common serving idea in recipe summaries).
burnOff: about 4.4 km of running (310 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.2 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 15 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: white bread is a wheat (grain) product and the recipe uses onion, chaat masala and table salt, which the common rule set avoids. Assumption: the common North and West India rule set.

ekadashi.reason: wheat bread is a grain, avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set, and the recipe has onion.

jain.reason: drop the potato, beetroot and onion and use more cucumber and tomato; the chutney must have no garlic or fresh ginger; check the bread label for added fat or additives.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; quick and light for iftar. Not a good sehri on its own: protein is only about 7 g (est.) and it is mostly refined bread.

jain.reason: drop the potato, beetroot and onion (all root vegetables) and use more cucumber and tomato (see Jain variant); no garlic or ginger in the chutney.

vegan.reason: the butter is dairy; use vegan butter or oil instead, and check the bread label, because some packaged breads contain milk.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so it contains no meat; no fish either.

sattvik.reason: leave out the 15 g onion (use extra cucumber); the chutney in this recipe has no garlic, but many street chutneys do.

glutenFree.reason: made with wheat bread. Use the Gluten-free variant, and note that most hing (asafoetida) sold in India is compounded with wheat flour (the main recipe uses none).

dairyFree.reason: the 15 g butter is dairy; swap for vegan butter or a plant oil, and check the bread label.
